A long g-descender and final short stroke follow MD under the cancellation. The r contour remains partly hidden, so the existing doubt is not removed.

The broad cancelled cluster before the live G has dark loops and long overstrikes, but its original contour and exact extent are not fully recoverable. C’s underlined G remains only a tentative representation of this covered ink.

The broad T and low following forms support Toute, but not every struck letter is isolated. The trailing looped/descending cluster is still unreadable as a definite word or label, so the following illegible unit is preserved.
The heavy horizontal bar conceals the earlier value; only a thin downward-curving terminal remnant is left. The original 3 candidate is not resolved from that remnant.
The initial low descender and obscured humps under the long strike are compatible with genre but cannot all be recovered independently.
The lower l-loop, p-descender and later d-like rise support le poids, but shared crossings and the descender from the upper replacement hide part of the middle letters.
A p-like descender and low ending survive the cancellation below multiplicité. The other crossed loops do not establish every letter of espace.
A mostly horizontal shaft ends in a one-sided short downward turn. The literal dash is favoured, but a compressed arrowhead cannot be excluded; the uncertainty is over the whole relation stroke.

In the cancelled pinning phrase there is only one recoverable horizontal stroke, continuous with the cancellation. Plain G is favoured; an earlier underline coincident with that strike remains possible.

notes.text: The sheet headed 25 starts section 7 on the hatted M-G objects of dimension at most 2 and then treats dimension 0. It presents four equivalent conditions: the dimension statement, zero modular dimension expressed by the edge count reaching 3(g-1)+nu, minimality for the relation of générisation with the indicated morphisms being isomorphisms, and genus-zero vertices of order at most 3 with marked weight 3 minus the order. The page then claims uniqueness of a standard pinned curve over an arbitrary base and writes (60), M-G equals M-hat-G isomorphic to Spec Z equals S-zero, followed by (61), M-[G] isomorphic to the classifying object B(Gamma over S-zero). The side annotation names Gamma as Aut of the underlined G. This summarizes the author’s statements only; no equivalence or uniqueness proof has been checked.

Minimal and the two occurrences of générisation are clear readings, and the abbreviations tt and isom and spelling standart are retained. The inserted pinning label has a plain G; the later cancelled label favours plain G but may conceal an earlier underline. The connecting stroke in c remains dash/arrow uncertain. The accent in déf is visible in (60), and M1024 resolves to égal. All earlier covered word and symbol clusters remain uncertain, including the unreadable unit after Toute. The dark heading 25 and pencil 51 are both retained without assigning their ownership from this image.

coverage.differences_accounted: All 28 physical TSV rows were read, together with the full C and H fragments. Row 1 is scan/page-marker syntax. Rows 2–3 contain editorial framing of the title; the actual omitted heading 7 and first underline are change 01, while H’s editorial words are excluded. Rows 4–5 are the two title cancellations, changes 02–03. Rows 6–7 are leq/geq-style syntax and the closing editorial quotation. Row 8 is the Et prefix, change 05, which also accounts for H’s capital La. Rows 9–10 are quote-delimiter typography with the same quoted scope and need no separate row. Row 11 is the cancelled cluster and live plain G, change 06. Row 12 is certainty only: M1024 resolves to égal with no collation row. Rows 13–17 are the cancelled opening, minimal, first générisation, tt, second générisation and graph relation, changes 07–12. Row 18 is the tentative cancelled numeral, change 13. Row 19 is leq macro syntax. Rows 20–21 are one overlapping weight-revision place, change 14. Rows 22–25 are alors, isom, standart and the non-existent separate comma at the inserted phrase, changes 15–16 and 18–19. Row 26 is the accent in déf, change 22. Row 27 is the opening side-note revision, change 23. Row 28 combines pencil 51 and H’s extra terminal period, changes 25–26. Full-source comparison additionally catches the incorrect inclusion of Les in H’s strike (04), H’s strike of trouver (17), the ornamental base S (20), the uncertain decoration of the cancelled G (21), and H’s insertion state for pour le (24). Both witnesses underline the inserted G, which the ink does not support (19). Math braces, hats’ macro names, font conventions for Z, spacing, display wrappers, emphasis-to-underline conventions and H’s editorial title prose do not by themselves generate rows. All ten C doubt places are covered in decisions; M1024 is resolved and all other covered ink remains doubtful. Added dash/arrow and cancelled-G decoration uncertainties have their own decisions. The whole original and each newly made native half were viewed once; all nineteen crops were inspected once. Blind boxes cover every insertion, cancellation, margin note, differing word, less-than-high-confidence change, complete expression with a C/final mathematical doubt, and all 21 handwritten numeral groups including Roman I, the tentative struck numeral, every lower 0/1, both formula numbers and both pagination numbers. No additional margin writing, drawings or diagrams were found. Line count 29 comprises 23 main physical rows, four side-annotation rows and two pagination rows; interlinear replacements are inventoried with their host rows rather than counted twice.
